description: This program elective covers different types of energy storage systems, which may be stand-alone or grid connected, and their storage efficiency.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Energy Storage
syllabus.body: Relevance and scenario, perspective on the development of energy storage systems, energy storage criteria, general concepts, conventional batteries - fundamentals and applications.

syllabus.title: Grid-connected and Thermal Storage
syllabus.body: Grid-connected and off-grid energy storage systems and requirements. Thermal storage: thermal properties of materials, principle of operation, efficiency factors, large scale and medium scale operations, pros and cons, advances in thermal storage.

syllabus.title: Mechanical, Electrochemical and Fuel Cell Storage
syllabus.body: Mechanical storage - types of systems, principle of operation, emerging advances, case study on flywheels. Electrochemical storage - materials, principle of operation, positive and negative electrode materials, electrolytes. Fuel cells and hydrogen storage - principle of operation, challenges and case studies.

syllabus.title: Magnetic, Optical and Supercapacitor Storage
syllabus.body: Magnetic storage - principle of operation, emerging challenges, devices and technology review. Electro-optic and optical storage - principles of operation, device fabrication, emerging devices. Supercapacitors - principle of operation, device fabrication, challenges and technical review.

outcomes: Understand different types of storage technologies.
Design a thermal storage system and model a battery storage system.
Analyze the thermodynamics of a fuel cell and the appropriate storage technologies for different applications.
textbooks: John T. Warner, Handbook of Lithium-Ion Battery Pack Design: Chemistry, Components, Types and Terminology, Elsevier.
San Ping Jiang, Fundamentals and Applications of Lithium-Ion Battery Management in Electric Drive Vehicles, Wiley.
Kazunori Ozawa (ed.), Lithium Ion Rechargeable Batteries, Wiley.
referenceBooks: T. E. Lipman and A. Z. Weber, Fuel Cells and Hydrogen Production, Springer Reference.
Mehrdad Ehsani, Yimin Gao, Sebastien E. Gay and Ali Emadi, Modern Electric, Hybrid Electric and Fuel Cell Vehicles: Fundamentals, Theory and Design, CRC Press.
